question: Who should decide how much power and land the AI boom is allowed to use?
reflection: Technology serves humanity best when communities have a voice in what it costs them.

one_line: US politics is turning against data centres just as companies get more AI work done for the same money, putting pressure on the AI spending boom.

top_stories.title: US midterms put AI rules back on the table
top_stories.what: After Democrats won Congress, tech stocks fell and lawmakers signalled bills on data-centre power costs, independent model testing and company liability.
top_stories.why: Independent testing and liability rules in the US would shape the standards Gulf regulators and buyers expect from AI vendors.

top_stories.title: Political bias in an open model is easy to strip out
top_stories.what: Nous Research retrained Alibaba's open Qwen model into Arete-27B and says pro-Beijing answers fell from about 22% to under 1% with no loss in general skill.
top_stories.why: If a model's values can be reshaped with modest training, any organisation deploying open models should test them for bias on locally sensitive topics.

top_stories.title: Firms use more AI but spend about the same
top_stories.what: Spending data from the card firm Ramp reportedly shows AI usage still rising while customer spending grew only 1.5% over two months, thanks to price cuts and discounts.
top_stories.why: Cheaper AI makes large-scale text and survey analysis affordable for smaller public projects.

saudi_lens.text: As US communities resist new data centres over power and water, Saudi Arabia's offer of land, energy and fast approvals becomes more attractive to AI builders.
The Arete work shows that Arabic-language models deployed in the Kingdom can and should be checked for whose values they reflect.

idea.title: Values audit for Arabic AI answers
idea.pitch: Build a short test set of culturally and socially sensitive questions and compare how several models answer them in Arabic and English.
idea.fit: Government digital services, culture sector, consultancy
idea.first_step: Write 20 test questions with a panel of three colleagues and agree on what a balanced answer looks like.
